meta.method: Every chapter+layer that has both a he-jerusalem-1956 and an en-bb file was paired. Items were aligned positionally and the alignment was validated by requiring the (n, order, anchorId) key sequence to be identical on both sides. Candidate English renderings were mined by lift scoring of 1-3 gram frequencies inside the subset of aligned items containing a given Hebrew term, then each candidate was confirmed by reading real aligned pairs. Every citation below was extracted programmatically from the aligned corpus, not written by hand.

conventions.rule: A Hebrew letter used as an inline marker (א׳, ב׳ … ק, ר, ש, ת) is rendered as its gematria value in Arabic numerals: א→1 … ט→9, י→10, כ→20, ל→30, מ→40, נ→50, ס→60, ע→70, פ→80, צ→90, ק→100, ר→200, ש→300, ת→400. Never keep the Hebrew letter, never renumber sequentially.
conventions.evidence: 51 marker pairs across the four chapters that carry anchors; 51/51 follow the gematria mapping with no exception.

conventions.rule: ב"ה (ברוך הוא) after א"ס is always dropped: 'א"ס ב"ה' → 'Ein Sof'. ית' / יתברך is dropped or absorbed into 'His'/'Him'. ח"ו (חס ושלום) becomes the adverb 'whatsoever' in negative clauses, or is dropped — it is never rendered 'God forbid'. ע"ש / עש"ה (עיין שם) is usually dropped. ז"ל / זצ"ל do not occur anywhere in the aligned Hebrew, so no rendering is attested for them.
conventions.evidence: 79 occurrences of ב"ה in the aligned Hebrew; 0 occurrences of 'blessed' in en-bb. 206 occurrences of ית' with no dedicated English token. 12 rows with ח"ו; those rendered use 'whatsoever'.

conventions.rule: A transliterated term is followed by a square-bracketed English gloss on its first appearance in an item, then used bare: 'Rosh [head]', 'Guf [body]', 'Sof [end/conclusion]', 'Ein Sof [infinity]', 'Katnut [smallness/infancy]', 'Gadlut [greatness/adulthood]', 'Partzufim [pl. of Partzuf]', 'Klipot [shells]', 'Peh [mouth]', 'Hotem [nose]', 'Ozen [ear]', 'Nekudot [dots]', 'RTS [Rosh-Toch-Sof]'. The gloss is optional and is used sparsely — do not gloss on every occurrence.

knownGaps: en-bb covers 737 of the 5,148 Hebrew source chapters (14%) and only 4 of the 25 Hebrew commentary chapters. Parts 4 and 7-16 have no en-bb text at all, so no terminology from those parts is evidenced here.

Coverage is dominated by the Tables of Questions and Answers, which are terminological by nature. Only 6 running chapters (part-01/chapter-01, part-01/chapter-02, part-03/chapter-03, part-05/chapter-32 and their commentary layers) are aligned, so prose-level style evidence is much thinner than term-level evidence.

Terms requested in the brief but not evidenced strongly enough to lock: תע"ס and אדר"ז do not occur in the aligned Hebrew at all; ס"ה occurs once; זצ"ל occurs zero times, so no honorific rendering is attested for it.
עיבור, יניקה, דבקות, תגין each occur in 1-3 aligned items — too thin to lock and therefore omitted rather than guessed.
The 9 fallback chapters were aligned only at whole-chapter granularity, so citations drawn from them (marked 'whole-chapter (item counts differ)') are weaker evidence than item-level ones.

Frequency counts in `variants` are occurrence counts inside the subset of aligned items whose Hebrew matches the term's pattern; they are not corpus-wide counts and a single item can contribute several.
The en-ai version was deliberately not mined. It was only checked against the finished glossary; see the audit reported alongside this file.
